purpose: Unmodified RC39 classical state learner and existing RC39 W-method on independently authored, real protocol extracted transition models. This tests transfer from synthetic human-constructed 24 to external real-world Mealy machines; not new neural structure, not cross-formalism Q6.
provenance: Public external MQTT DOT models were browsed by researcher before this prereg; NOT blind-to-researcher. The original learner source and W-method were hash frozen before these external files were examined in this turn. Exact compiled executable output has never been scored on these 3 models in this project.
machine_model: Resettable complete deterministic Mealy; trust external DOT model as reference and publication-independent source. Alphabet encoding assigned by sorted labels only; raw names not used for policy choice. Reference state graph NOT given to learner or W tester; graph used only in the source membership backend and in independent after-freeze proof.
primary_gate: Three distinct external DOT blob hashes and models, all 3 executable learned ASTs independently product-equivalent on all finite inputs, no false certificates, mutated model rejected, query costs and cpu recorded. No success threshold on query efficiency vs arbitrary other baseline.
negative_control: Flip an emitted initial-state output and independently reject the mutation. Reject broken DOT, incorrect pinned blob, incomplete transition model and query-budget exhaustion. The completeness theorem REQUIRES a correct externally trusted state bound; if bound is wrong, this implementation cannot guarantee detecting that mistake by membership alone.
baseline: Unchanged pre-external RC39 L* + W is classical. No neural source policy, no claims of improvement over strongest classical software. A passive zero-query baseline is incomplete; not used for performance superiority claims.
note: No original ARC-AGI-1 evaluation IDs; no external .dot bytes are committed; fetch three pinned paths and verify original Git blobs at runtime. Preserve first success or failure without favorable rewrite.
